Thirteen functions call `async_op` directly, all in `tokio/src`. I searched the whole repository for `async_op` and matched each call site to the function that contains it. Every call is written as `trace::async_op(...)`:

- **`time/interval.rs`**: `Interval::tick` (line 437)
- **`sync/rwlock.rs`**: `read` (450), `read_owned` (598), `write` (792), `write_owned` (927)
- **`sync/barrier.rs`**: `Barrier::wait` (127)
- **`sync/oneshot.rs`**: `Sender::closed` (706)
- **`sync/semaphore.rs`**: `acquire` (581), `acquire_many` (628), `acquire_owned` (763), `acquire_many_owned` (827)
- **`sync/mutex.rs`**: `lock` (446), `lock_owned` (629)

The other places where `async_op` appears are not calls to this function. In `sleep.rs`, `oneshot.rs` and `batch_semaphore.rs` it is part of tracing span or target names. The tests under `tests/tracing-instrumentation` only match those span names.
